etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Medieval Latin dīvergō (“bend away from, go in a different direction”), from Latin dī- + vergō (“bend”).
senses: (intransitive, literally, of lines or paths) To run apart; to separate; to tend into different directions.
(intransitive, figuratively, of interests, opinions, or anything else) To become different; to run apart; to separate; to tend into different directions.
A point where a lane branches off from the main flow.
